canonical_definition: Long-Context Handling refers to the ability of models to retain, utilize, and reason over extended input histories or generate long outputs without degradation in performance, often involving mitigation of context-length limitations, attention dilution, or "lost in the middle" failures. While some definitions emphasize maintaining effective attention mechanisms or position-aware scaling as context length increases, others focus on operational challenges like handling iterative feedback, video-language histories, or sequence modeling beyond fixed window limits. Disagreements arise in scope, with certain works narrowing the construct to input/output length constraints, while others address broader memory and attention dynamics in long-sequence tasks.
